fact_lines: Nine beaches and four ocean pools,|including Sydney's longest stretch|of undeveloped sand (4.8 km).|Reachable by train from the city.
Framed by the 1900-built Bathurst|Lighthouse. White sand turns pink in|low afternoon light, and a coral|reef close to shore suits snorkellers.
Reached on a 2.2 km return walk over|a ridge in Cape Hillsborough National|Park. Steep forest encloses the cove,|and Cascade Creek crosses the beach.
Seven km of undeveloped sand south of|Cape Byron, in Arakwal National Park.|Named for tallow that washed ashore|after an 1864 shipwreck.
Thought to be named after St Elmo's|fire, a bluish glow that can appear|above ships' masts. A secluded bay|between rocky headlands.
Little penguins come ashore here at|dusk, watched from a platform lit with|red light. Nearby rises The Nut,|a 143 m volcanic plug.
A narrow finger of sand built up by|wind and waves. It's the departure|point for 4WD barges to K'gari, and|a popular beach camping spot.
A 2 km beach split by Balcombe Creek,|known for its bathing boxes. Beach|matting for accessibility is laid|daily from November to May.
Named by Matthew Flinders in 1802|for the smoke of Aboriginal fires he|saw onshore. Today an oyster-growing|town with a long timber jetty.
An inland waterhole, 80 km west of|Alice Springs, carved out by floods.|Known to the Arrernte as Udepata.|Its water is cold even in summer.
